catalog_quote: 尼苏普是彝族内部一个小支系的名称。尼苏彝语最大特点是辅音多元音少，元音松紧对立。3个声调，每个声调都出现松紧元音。在尼苏彝语中至今还保留一套完整的tl、tlh、dl、ndlh塞边音。这组音与彝语各大方言都有整齐的对应。

new_statements.translation: Nisupu [Nyisuphu] is the name of a small branch within the Yi nationality. The most salient features of Nisu [Nyisu] Yi are that it has many consonants and few vowels, and a tense/lax vowel opposition. There are 3 tones, and tense and lax vowels both occur under every tone. Nisu Yi still preserves a complete set of lateral-release stops tl, tlh, dl, ndlh. This set of sounds corresponds regularly across all the major Yi dialects.

new_statements.relation_note: 3 tones; tense/lax vowels under every tone; large consonant inventory incl. lateral-release stops tl tlh dl ndlh; few vowels.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Nyisuphu (Shilin 'Nisu' Yi) is a tone language with three lexical tones; the tense/lax vowel contrast is independent of tone (both phonation types occur with each of the three tones). Nothing is said about word stress/accent.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog's own bibliography codes this article as language code 'Nyisu of Shilin county [NOCODE_Nyisu]' and it is one of the three references on the nyis1235 page; the abstract's 尼苏普 (Nisupu = ȵi55su33pʰu55 'Nyisuphu') 'a small branch within the Yi' is the Shilin (Gaohanshan village) group that Glottolog's coordinates (24.69 N 103.60 E) denote, not the large Southern-Yi Nisu. Caveat: Glottolog's languoid also absorbs the Fumin/Anning Yellow Yi (Nyisupho, a Nosoid/Adur-like Northern Yi lect per Bradley 1999/2007), which this article does not describe; whether the two are the same language is unresolved (Wikipedia: 'not known').

sources.note: Identity only: Yellow Yi, <300 speakers (Bradley 2005, 2007), 4 villages in NW Fumin and 1 in NW Anning, migrated from Sichuan, 'most closely related to Suondi Yi according to Bradley (2005)'; Shilin Nyisu (Gaohanshan village, Zhuqing township) documented in Wu 1997 and YNYF 1984; 'It is not known whether Nyisu of Shilin and Nyisu of Kunming are closely related.' Nothing on stress.

sources.note: Nyisu occurs only as a 2003 elicitation point in Table 3.1 (p. 67: 'Nyisupo [ȵi55su33pho21] EY Lu Cuiling 25 06/07 Luomian TW, Fumin CT, YN 富民县罗免乡'); sec. 3.6 (p. 67) says only Gepu, Samu, Lipo, Maang and Azha of those points are used, so no Nyisu inventory or profile is given. The words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur anywhere in the thesis; sec. 4.4.1 (p. 88) gives only 'tonemes are from 3 to 8' for Nisoic generally. SILENT on Nyisu and on stress.

sources.note: Nothing Nyisu-specific. Only family-level: 'all Ngwi languages share an innovative two-way tonal contrast in original stop-final syllables; the Northern Ngwi languages have mostly reversed phonetic values for these two tones'; Nyisu is 'quite similar to the southern Adur dialect of Nosu', moribund (~300 speakers of 1,200), 'some suggest that the Nyisu are escaped slaves of the Nosu'. No stress/accent content.
